inspection: All twelve original anonymous PNGs viewed at full-frame 1920x1080. Image hashes read only for evidence identity; mapping, source candidate filenames, parameters and implementation not inspected.
evidenceType: Same-scene direct Editor diagnostic renders, not native gameplay acceptance
rankingOrder: Best rank group first; labels within a group are tied

cam_hill.confidence: high for A/B over C; low for distinguishing A from B
cam_hill.reason: A and B retain dark olive living-leaf identity and coherent crown mass. C introduces a pale blue-gray/silver speckled appearance, particularly across upper and right clusters, that weakens the canopy's mass. C exposes more bright fine detail without a corresponding convincing improvement in volumetric leaf/branch separation.

cam_hero.confidence: low confidence in any separation; no defensible material winner
cam_hero.reason: All three preserve olive color, sunlit patches and the same readable main limbs. Dense upper/interior clusters remain similar dark masses. Any small differences are below the level at which I can justify a reliable preferred version in these full-frame images.

cam_tree_canopy_below.confidence: low confidence in any separation; no demonstrated shade-readability improvement
cam_tree_canopy_below.reason: The broad shaded clusters at upper left and right remain dark olive and difficult to separate internally in all three. Sky holes and large branches remain legible; small branches embedded in foliage do not gain a clearly meaningful readable layer. No broad glow or gross coverage loss is apparent.

cam_tree_canopy_edge.confidence: low confidence in any separation; no demonstrated shade-readability improvement
cam_tree_canopy_edge.reason: All three keep the same crown outline and green/olive leaf response. Central shaded fronds still merge into dense textured sheets with tangled thin branch lines. Differences do not support a reliable quality ranking or a claim that the shaded-canopy defect is fixed.

recommendation: Do not promote a shade variant on these images. Retain the repaired edge treatment as an independent earlier preference. After lock/reveal, validate that each intended candidate reached the recorded rendered material, then recapture only if that audit identifies an evidence problem. Otherwise change the shade-response approach rather than claiming a barely visible parameter difference solves it.
rejectionReasons: Shaded leaf clusters still merge, especially below and at canopy edge.
One hill candidate has visibly poorer pale blue-gray/silver response.
Fine leaves remain noisy in these direct Editor captures; this cannot determine native MSAA or temporal quality.
Near bark remains soft and low in readable shaded surface structure.
No native temporal or performance qualification is established.

arkReference.preference: Official ARK Scorched Earth courtyard still looks more finished overall and in differentiated foliage response
arkReference.limitations: Different subjects/species, lens, lighting and unknown reference hardware/settings/promotional processing; not a performance, temporal or physics comparison.
